LEVEL 2 HEALTH AND SAFETY

Safety signs

Recognise the message. Understand the hazard. Choose the right response.

Four categoriesSign libraryOn-site decisionsCOSHH pictograms

The four main categories

Use the colour, shape and symbol together. In this resource, Information means the green safe-condition signs used for safety routes and facilities.

Prohibition

You must not

Red circle and diagonal bar

Warning

There is a hazard

Yellow triangle with black border

Mandatory

You must

Blue circle with white symbol

Information / safe condition

Safety routes and facilities

Green square or rectangle

One extra category: red square or rectangular signs identify fire equipment. A red circle with a diagonal bar prohibits an action.

How to read a sign

  1. Recognise the category. Use colour and shape.
  2. Identify the message. Look at the symbol and read the wording.
  3. Check where it applies. It may mark a doorway, a route, equipment or a whole area.
  4. Follow the instruction. Use the controls, PPE and local procedure for your task.

Memory aid: Red circle = STOP the action. Yellow triangle = CAUTION. Blue circle = MUST. Green = SAFETY location or route.

Common signs and their meanings

ProhibitionWarningMandatoryInformation / safe conditionFire equipment

Prohibition

Red circle and diagonal bar. You must not. Black symbol on white. The diagonal red bar shows that the action is forbidden.

No smoking

Keep smoking materials away from the marked area.

Smoking and naked flames forbidden

Keep flames and other ignition sources away.

No unauthorised access

Enter only with permission.

No pedestrians

Use an approved alternative pedestrian route.

No industrial vehicles

Keep forklifts and similar vehicles out.

Do not touch

Leave the equipment or surface alone.

Not drinking water

Do not drink from this supply.

Do not extinguish with water

Water is prohibited for firefighting here. Follow the fire procedure.

Warning

Yellow triangle with black border. There is a hazard. A black symbol identifies the danger. Read any accompanying wording and follow the controls for the work.

Electrical hazard

Keep clear of electrical hazards. Follow authorised safe electrical work procedures.

General warning

Read the accompanying wording to identify the specific hazard.

Trip hazard

Watch the route and report or deal with obstructions under local procedures.

Drop or fall hazard

Keep clear of edges and follow barriers.

Industrial vehicles

Use designated pedestrian routes and stay visible to drivers.

Suspended load

Stay outside the lifting exclusion zone.

Flammable material

Keep ignition sources away and follow storage rules.

Corrosive material

Avoid contact and follow handling instructions.

Toxic material

Avoid exposure and follow the task assessment.

Explosive material

Follow access restrictions and site procedures.

Oxidising material

Can intensify fire. Follow storage and separation rules.

Biological hazard

Follow hygiene and exposure controls.

Laser beam

Follow access and exposure controls for the equipment.

Radioactive material / ionising radiation

Follow restricted access and specialist instructions.

Non-ionising radiation

Follow the stated access and exposure controls.

Strong magnetic field

Check restrictions for implants and equipment before entering.

Low temperature

Follow cold-exposure and handling precautions.

Mandatory

Blue circle with white symbol. You must. The sign requires a particular action. PPE must suit the task and the risk assessment.

Wear a safety helmet

Wear the specified helmet in the marked area.

Wear eye protection

Use suitable eye protection for the task.

Wear hearing protection

Fit the specified ear defenders or earplugs.

Wear protective gloves

Use the glove type specified for the hazard.

Wear safety footwear

Wear suitable protective footwear for the area and task.

Wear protective clothing

Use the specified protective clothing.

Wear respiratory protection

Use the specified equipment with the required training and fit.

Wear face protection

Use a suitable face shield where required.

Wear a safety harness

Use the specified fall-protection system with suitable training.

Pedestrians must use this route

Follow the designated pedestrian route.

General mandatory action

Read and carry out the accompanying instruction.

Information / safe condition

Green square or rectangle. Safety routes and facilities. White symbols identify emergency escape routes, first aid or other safety facilities.

Escape route to the left

Follow the arrow to the left and continue along the signed route.

Escape route to the right

Follow the arrow to the right and continue along the signed route.

First aid

Shows first aid facilities or assistance.

Emergency eyewash

Know where the eyewash station is located.

Stretcher

Shows where emergency transport equipment is kept.

Assembly point

Go to the designated point after evacuation and follow roll-call instructions.

Safety shower

Shows the location of an emergency shower.

Emergency telephone

Shows a telephone for first aid or escape assistance.

Fire equipment

Red square or rectangle. Equipment location. White symbols on red identify firefighting equipment and alarm facilities.

Fire extinguisher

Shows the equipment location. Use only within your training and local procedure.

Fire alarm call point

Shows where to raise the alarm.

Fire hose

Identifies firefighting equipment.

Signs in an electrical workshop

A workshop entrance can display several signs. Permission controls access. The lightning symbol warns about electricity. The blue goggles sign requires eye protection. Each sign adds a different instruction or warning.

Before work: check authorisation and supervision, read the task assessment and use the specified protection. Follow safe isolation and verification procedures where required. A warning sign does not prove equipment is isolated.
Scenario 1: a damaged electrical warning sign

Report the damage. Clarify the hazard with your tutor or supervisor before work. Keep access restrictions and safe working procedures in place.

Scenario 2: a blue PPE sign at a cutting station

Wear the specified eye protection before starting. Check that it suits the task and fits correctly. Follow the machine instructions and supervision requirements.

Scenario 3: an alarm sounds near a green exit sign

Follow the signed escape route and local evacuation procedure. Go to the designated assembly point, follow roll-call instructions and wait for authorisation before returning.

Good sign use

Position and visibility

  • Signs need to be visible where people encounter the hazard or make a decision.
  • Keep signs readable, well lit and free from obstructions.
  • Report signs that are missing, damaged or unclear.
  • Learn the local routes and emergency facilities during induction.

Extra wording and arrows

  • Supplementary wording clarifies a symbol or gives a specific instruction.
  • A general warning symbol needs enough context to explain the hazard.
  • Follow the direction arrow on an escape sign.
  • Read all signs at an entrance before entering.

Safety signs communicate risks and required behaviour. Barriers, guards, safe systems of work and other controls still apply. Ask your tutor or supervisor if you are unsure.

COSHH: chemical hazard pictograms

COSHH means Control of Substances Hazardous to Health. Chemical labels use GB CLP pictograms: a black symbol on white inside a red diamond. These differ from yellow workplace warning triangles.

Gas under pressure

Gas cylinder. Contains gas under pressure.

Explosive

Exploding bomb. May explode under specified conditions.

Oxidising

Flame over a circle. May cause or intensify fire.

Flammable

Flame. May catch fire easily.

Corrosive

Liquid damaging a hand and metal. May cause severe skin burns, eye damage or corrosion of metals.

Health hazard / irritant

Exclamation mark. May cause effects such as irritation or harmful acute toxicity.

Acute toxicity

Skull and crossbones. Can cause severe acute poisoning.

Serious health hazard

Person with a star-shaped chest marking. Can indicate serious effects such as cancer, respiratory sensitisation or organ damage.

Hazardous to the environment

Dead tree and fish. May harm aquatic life.

Before use: read the complete label, check the safety data sheet and follow the COSHH assessment. One product may show several pictograms. The label identifies the precise hazards and precautions.

Some pictograms describe physical or environmental hazards as well as health hazards. Fire and explosion risks also need the relevant site controls.

Other safety messages

Chemical hazard labels

Chemical labels use black pictograms inside a red diamond on white. They differ from yellow workplace warning triangles. Read the complete label and follow the safety data and COSHH assessment before handling a substance.

The old yellow triangle with a black cross for “harmful or irritant” has been removed from the listed workplace signs. Use the appropriate current sign or chemical pictogram.

Barriers, alarms and signals

Safety communication can also use warning tape, illuminated signs, audible alarms, hand signals and verbal instructions. Learn what the local signals mean and respond according to the site procedure.

Restricted areas remain restricted even if nobody is working there at that moment.

Common mistakes

ConfusionCorrect interpretation
Every red sign means “do not”.Red circles prohibit. Red rectangles or squares identify fire equipment.
A warning triangle tells you what PPE to wear.The triangle identifies a hazard. A blue circle requires a particular action.
A green exit sign points towards fire equipment.Green escape signs show the escape route. Follow the arrow.
The sign makes the area safe.Follow the risk controls and local instructions as well as the sign.
